---
title: "Known limitations"
subtitle: "What DeskPets can't do yet, so you don't have to find out the hard way"
---

DeskPets is a personal project, and these are the gaps I know about.

## Platform and hardware

- **Windows only.** macOS and Linux are not supported or tested.
- **No CPU temperature.** Windows doesn't expose it through the library DeskPets uses, so the grumpy animation reacts to **GPU** temperature or swap instead.
- **NVIDIA GPUs only.** Other GPUs aren't read, so on a machine without an NVIDIA card, grumpy fires from swap alone and rarely.
- **Input means idle time.** DeskPets only knows how long it has been since you last touched the keyboard or mouse. It can't tell what you're doing, so *working together* means "you've been active lately", not "you're typing code".

## Behavior

- **The sad animation has no trigger.** It exists, but you can only see it from the tray's *Poke the pets* menu.
- **The thresholds are tuned to one machine.** The swap limit in particular is a guess that I haven't checked under real memory pressure. See [Configuration](/guide/configuration.qmd).
- **There is no global hotkey.** If you lose the pets in click-through mode, double-click the tray icon.

## Art

- **The jump has no lift.** The arc was lost when the frames were aligned.
- **The stroll ends with Layla leaving the frame,** so it plays once and holds its last pose.
- **Pixel art can look stretched** on displays scaled by 150%, because the sprites are drawn at whole-pixel sizes.

Details on the art issues are on [Art pipeline](/internals/art-pipeline.qmd).

## Not tested yet

Things a short test can't show: a long-running session, sleep and resume, multiple monitors, and sustained real-world load. If something misbehaves in one of those, please [open an issue](https://github.com/Suyash-Naik/DeskPets/issues).
